title: Japan Ku-area of Tokyo CPI (November 2026, preliminary), 08:30 JST — the 21-day pre-announcement of the national November print
source: EST: two independent Statistics Bureau surfaces, both fetched and parsed by this session on 2026-09-05. (1) stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes), whose single 17-row table parses row-by-row against the header 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks' as ['October', 'November 20', 'November', 'November 27', ''] — i.e. the Tokyo November-2026 preliminary CPI releases 2026-11-27. (2) stat.go.jp/data/kouhyou/e-stat_cpi.xml, the Bureau's own machine-readable 公表予定 feed (HTTP 200, 59,990 bytes, UTF-16LE), linked from its live Japanese results page and carrying its own update stamp of 2026-08-28 — eight days before this fetch. Its 東京都区部（中旬速報値） class lists '2026-11-27 08:30 | 2026年11月分'. THE 08:30 JST RELEASE TIME IS READ OFF THAT FEED, not asserted from convention: every one of the feed's 37 scheduled items carries release_hour 08 and release_minute 30. Filed estimate on two counts only — the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The staleness objection other Japan CPI entries carry (the English page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026') is answered by the XML feed, which was re-published 2026-08-28 and agrees with the English table on all 30 release dates.
notes: DISCOVERED during the japan-cpi-2026-12-18 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and tracked because it is the LEAD INDICATOR that FT-japan-cpi-2026-12-18-2 scores against: the Ku-area-of-Tokyo flash is a subsample of the national basket and pre-announces the national November print (2026-12-18) by 21 days. That lane measured how well, using the Bureau's own 2025-base monthly files (e-Stat statInfId=000040491314 for Japan and 000040491317 for Tokyo, fileKind=4, parsed locally out of the OOXML: 679 national observations 1970-01 to 2026-07 and 680 Tokyo 1970-01 to 2026-08). Differencing Tokyo's year-on-year against the national year-on-year for NOVEMBER MONTHS ONLY, on the BoJ's core measure (all items less fresh food): 2018 +0.11, 2019 +0.11, 2020 +0.23, 2021 -0.11, 2022 -0.14, 2023 -0.23, 2024 -0.33, 2025 -0.21 — mean -0.073pp, MEAN ABSOLUTE 0.183pp, worst month 0.33pp, 7 of 8 inside +/-0.3pp and 8 of 8 inside +/-0.35pp. That is tighter than the full 103-month sample the sibling japan-cpi-2027-01-22 lane measured (mean absolute 0.201pp, worst 0.85pp, 78% within +/-0.3pp) and tighter than December months (0.20pp, worst 0.64pp), which makes NOVEMBER THE TIGHTEST MONTH MEASURED ON THIS CALENDAR — on a sample of only eight, so it is a real ordering of the data that could still be noise. The practical consequence: the national print on 2026-12-18 is confirmation, not news, and this date is where the information actually arrives. Impact is LOW: symbols is empty and no house playbook is keyed to Japanese CPI; this entry's value is calibration and attribution rather than a trade. Registered against FT-japan-cpi-2026-12-18-2, which scores the Tokyo-to-national gap at a +/-0.3pp threshold — inherited unchanged from the sibling's FT-japan-cpi-2027-01-22-1 rather than fitted to November, so that the pair measures whether November really is tighter than December.
